agencies.name: Vietnam Environment Administration (VEA)
agencies.role: Issued the technical guidance for calculating the Vietnam Air Quality Index (VN_AQI).

nationalIndex.name: Vietnam Air Quality Index (VN_AQI)
nationalIndex.description: Set by Decision 1459/QD-TCMT of 12 November 2019. Six bands: 0 to 50 Tốt, 51 to 100 Trung bình, 101 to 150 Kém, 151 to 200 Xấu, 201 to 300 Rất xấu, 301 to 500 Nguy hại. Hourly AQI uses a NowCast of the last 12 hours for PM; daily AQI uses 24-hour means for PM2.5 and PM10.

monitoring.text: ASMC reported moderate transboundary haze over southern Vietnam in mid-September 2026, according to Bernama.

The Viet Nam Environment Agency says the ministry operates 37 air quality stations, with 16 more planned to reach 53 between 2026 and 2030. Readings are published on cem.gov.vn and the VnAir app, and the Envisoft system collects automatic station data.

seasonalPattern.text: In March 2025 satellite data showed extensive fire activity across Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam, Malay Mail reported.
The agency describes a PM2.5 season from about October or November to April, with straw burning near cities among the causes, and aims to end rice straw burning in the Red River Delta.

healthContext.text: Decision 1459 links each band to health advice. From 101 sensitive groups (older people, children, people with heart or lung disease) are affected; at 301 to 500 everyone should stay indoors with doors and windows closed.

policy.text: VEA Decision 1459/QD-TCMT introduced the current method for calculating VN_AQI.

dataAccess.name: Centre for Environmental Monitoring (cem.gov.vn) and VnAir app
dataAccess.note: Official VN_AQI readings are published on the website and app. No documented API or reuse licence was found when checked on 23 October 2026.

dataAccess.name: Envisoft (enviinfo.cem.gov.vn)
dataAccess.note: Named by VEA as the system that receives automatic station data. Public access terms not checked.

openQuestions: Whether cem.gov.vn or Envisoft offers a documented API and reuse licence has not been confirmed.
How often southern Vietnam is affected by transboundary haze from the south of the region is not established.
